result.title: What Do Collusion Probes Read? Three Pitfalls in Evaluating Multi-Agent Collusion Monitors
result.comment: 30 pages, 5 figures. Code: https://github.com/mainul3195/collusion-probe-pitfalls ; data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/mainul3195/collusion-probe-pitfalls ; archive: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23636508
result.summary: Activation probes look like near-perfect monitors for secret collusion among large language model (LLM) agents. We show that they mostly detect that an agent was told to collude, not that it decided to. Our benchmark (2,500 committee and 1,476 code-review episodes) adds agents who receive the collusion instruction and refuse it, separating instruction from decision. Published detectors barely tell colluders from these refusers, and our best probe separates them mostly by reading the instruction: without it, agent AUROC falls from 1.00 to 0.61. Two further pitfalls inflate reported results: scored after the vote, a rule that only reads the votes reaches AUROC 0.990 but finds nothing before it; and in 57% of attempts no colluder argues for the target in public. The decision is still there: a probe trained on agents' own choices reads it (AUROC 0.73 without the instruction), and probes find colluders whose goal was fine-tuned into the weights (AUROC 0.995; pre-registered). We turn the controls into a protocol for testing any collusion monitor, and adapt scan statistics into an online monitor for groups of any size.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建带「收到共谋指令但拒绝」控制组的多智能体共谋基准（约 2,500 个委员会与 1,476 个代码评审回合），发现已发表的激活探针主要读取「被指示共谋」而非「决定共谋」，并指出投票后打分、公开辩护缺失等评估陷阱，进而给出监测器测试协议与可在任意规模群体上运行的在线扫描统计监测器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「指令 vs 决策」对照设计和探针实际读取内容的归因分析，可供核查 LVR 中「latent 状态保留视觉证据或推理决策」的结论是否只是读到了输入提示，也可为贡献分配与评测控制提供参照；但论文属纯文本多智能体监控，迁移需自行判断。
